title: 12th Sitting of First session of 2026
summary: The sitting opened at 10:01 and closed at 12:00 on Monday 27 April 2026. The chair announced that the government had taken back its bill amending the law on preventing sexual abuse and harassment, and a constitutional amendment bill from Mohamed Ibrahim (North Galolhu) had its first reading. Most of the sitting was a debate on a motion by Meekail Ahmed Nasym (MDP) asking MPs for their views on whether Public Service Media gave the MDP a fair chance to be heard. MDP members and one MDA member backed it, PNC members opposed it, and the sitting ended with the debate unfinished and no vote taken.

items.title: Opening prayer and start of the sitting
Attendance of members
items.outcome: 38 present, 7 on leave, 1 on official travel reported by the chair

items.title: Announcement of the day's agenda (agenda no. 2026/1/12)
Government bill amending the Law on Prevention of Sexual Abuse and Harassment (Law 16/2014), submitted via Abdulla Shareef (Kelaa)
items.outcome: chair announced the bill was taken back by the government on 26 April 2026 for further amendments

items.title: Bill to amend the Constitution, submitted by Mohamed Ibrahim (North Galolhu)
Motion by Meekail Ahmed Nasym (South Galolhu) seeking MPs' views on Public Service Media and equal airtime for the MDP
items.outcome: debated, not finished when the sitting ended; no vote

speakers.name: Ibrahim Shujau
positions: Opposed the motion, calling it a campaign tool based on untrue claims, and urged the MDP to be responsible.
Cited emails and calls to parties offering airtime in February 2026, and a count of 112 MDP news items against 121 for the PNC.
Said the government has repaid large debts, which public media should report, and that the motion wastes the Majlis's time.

speakers.name: Meekail Ahmed Nasym
positions: As mover, said Public Service Media is legally bound to give parties equal chances but gave the MDP no platform in the recent campaigns.
Said the state broadcaster acted as a media wing for one side and that the Majlis must hold public bodies to account.

speakers.name: Mohamed Abbas
positions: Supported the motion and said state media has been used for political propaganda under past governments, with few viewers.
Said cost of living and the tourism slowdown are hurting people and the media does not report it.
Raised Velidhoo land reclamation, saying it is not in the budget or land use plan, and stalled local projects.

speakers.name: Mohamed Musthafa Ibrahim
positions: Said public media must report government and state institutions' work, that all parties were treated equally in elections, and that no motion or debate is needed.

speakers.name: Mauroof Zakir
positions: Thanked the mover and supported the motion, citing the Public Service Media Act and election law on equal treatment.
Said MPs must hold bodies accountable when they do not follow the law, and linked it to cutting state spending.

speakers.name: Abdul Gafoor Moosa
positions: Raised a point of order saying the Baarashu member was making false claims about what the MDP chairperson had said.

speakers.name: Hussain Shareef
positions: Called the motion groundless and said he would not support it.
Said the broadcaster's duty is to inform citizens of government work, and criticised street protests and abusive language shown live.
Said the government has repaid large debts, which the media should report.

speakers.name: Ibrahim Muhammad
positions: Called the motion a campaign strategy aimed at discrediting state institutions and said he would not vote for it.
Said he had never been promoted on Public Service Media as a government-side member.

speakers.name: Ibrahim Falah
positions: Said the motion is false and tied to the MDP chairperson contest, and that Public Service Media covers all parties' debates equally.
Said the MDP could call the broadcaster's officials to committees but has not.
Said about 900 million US dollars of debt was repaid within a month, and that the Elections Commission should review party street activity.

speakers.name: Dr. Ahmed Shamheed
positions: Said the MDP parliamentary group met the broadcaster's management on 7 April, raised concerns before filing, and got no response.
Said coverage of the 12 April sitting left out MDP views on the bill debated.
Said the Public Service Media Act requires independence and equal chances, and urged the government to follow the law.

speakers.name: Abdul Sattar Mohamed
positions: Opposed the motion, saying the broadcaster's news follows its law and the motion names no specific breach.
Said MPs can call broadcaster officials to committees, and that the broadcaster's own figures show party airtime.

speakers.name: Hassan Mufeed Abdul Gadir
positions: Opposed the motion and said street protests should not be carried by the broadcaster if they spread unrest.
Urged the mover not to use the Majlis floor for his party chairperson campaign.

speakers.name: Ali Moosa
positions: Opposed the motion, saying its main points concern the council election result and promotion claims.
Recalled the 2023 presidential election coverage, which he said favoured the then president's results.
Cited the 2024 broadcaster audit report, including a reported 10.3 million rufiyaa loss, as a more pressing matter.

decisions: The chair announced that the government took back the amendment bill to the Law on Prevention of Sexual Abuse and Harassment (16/2014) on 26 April 2026 for further amendments.
The bill to amend the Constitution submitted by Mohamed Ibrahim (North Galolhu) had its first reading.
The sitting ended with the debate on the Public Service Media motion unfinished; the next sitting was set for Tuesday 28 April 2026 at 9:00.
